headline: Rockstar Games responds to GTA 6 leaks, calls it "heartbreaking" for the team
summary: Rockstar Games issued its first official statement after extensive Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay leaks, describing the incident as "heartbreaking." An "extended look" at the game will stream tomorrow on Netflix, with the full game releasing November 19th.
details: Rockstar Games has released its first official statement regarding the recent Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay leaks. The studio called the period "heartbreaking for our team," expressing disappointment over how the game was revealed to the public.

The company stated, "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time." They also apologized for the prolonged development, promising to share more details and official gameplay soon.
Fans can expect an "extended look" at the game tomorrow, streaming exclusively on Netflix at 3 PM ET. The highly anticipated game itself is set to launch on November 19th.

Rockstar thanked the community for their support, emphasizing that they are making the game for the fans. They hope players will wait to experience the game fully on its release date, despite potential spoilers from the leaks.

headline_marked: [[d-Matrix stacks AI accelerator directly on custom DRAM]] for 100 TB/s per card at Hot Chips 2026
headline: d-Matrix stacks AI accelerator directly on custom DRAM for 100 TB/s per card at Hot Chips 2026
summary: d-Matrix unveiled Raptor, a 3D DRAM accelerator delivering 100 TB/s bandwidth from 32GB per card. It features a TSMC 4nm compute die bonded face-to-face on a custom DRAM die.
details: d-Matrix presented Raptor at Hot Chips 2026, introducing it as the first 3D DRAM accelerator for generative inference. It features a TSMC 4nm compute die bonded face-to-face on a custom DRAM die, delivering 100 TB/s of bandwidth from 32GB per card.

The vertical interface boasts an energy cost of 0.37 pJ/bit, significantly lower than the 2.4 pJ/bit for HBM4. This design projects around 4.7 times higher throughput per card compared to HBM-based solutions, based on working silicon measurements.

While CEO Sid Sheth mentioned a 2027 launch to CNBC, d-Matrix provided no firm date, volume, or pricing information at Hot Chips. All performance figures, including 988 tokens/second on the Kimi K3 model, are projections from early silicon.

Raptor inverts the typical 3D stacking, placing the logic die on top and DRAM underneath, allowing a cold plate to sit directly on the compute silicon. The DRAM die also functions as an interposer, carrying PCIe and die-to-die signals through its TSVs, enabling the high bandwidth.

The one-high stack achieves a power density of 0.5W/mm², manageable with liquid cooling. The DRAM is designed for a 105°C junction temperature, which requires an eight times higher refresh rate due to reduced retention, a penalty d-Matrix absorbed by shrinking microbanks.

The die incorporates 840 banks per chiplet, with 72 spare banks wired into a two-level mux chain for fault tolerance. A [132,128] Reed-Solomon code on the logic die corrects two symbol errors per 128 bytes, further enhancing reliability.

The custom interface lacks a PHY or burst structure, necessitating a unique inversion tag to recover I/O power. This co-design of bank geometry, spare-bank mux tree, refresh behavior, and ECC columns is crucial for the 0.37 pJ/bit figure, as no standard memory maker offers such a die.

d-Matrix has named TSMC and Alchip as partners but has not disclosed the custom DRAM manufacturer. This comes during a period of extreme DRAM market tightness, with prices estimated to rise over 400% by late 2026 and HBM4 lines sold out, posing a significant challenge for a startup seeking bespoke dies.
